about: Chapter 6, The Dairy Farm: 69 patterns, four for each of the 15 skills (1 and 2 marks), three 3-mark and three 5-mark written questions, and three 4-mark case studies, drawn from the chapter's 500 questions. All DRAFT until Ashalatha approves them.

patterns.text: A shape stands for a number. If {a} × shape = {a * b}, what number is hidden?
patterns.hint: Which number, multiplied by {a}, gives {a * b}?
patterns.explanation: {a} × {b} = {a * b}, so the hidden number is {b}.
patterns.misconception: Tests only one clue or treats the two factors as interchangeable with the product.
patterns.notes: First factor 3 to 9, hidden factor 4 to 12 (different).

patterns.text: I am a multiple of {m}, greater than {lo}, less than {hi}, and I am {par}. Which number am I?
patterns.hint: List the multiples of {m} between {lo} and {hi}, then use the last clue.
patterns.explanation: The multiples of {m} between {lo} and {hi} are {x} and {x + m}. Only {ans} is {par}.
patterns.misconception: Tests only one clue or treats the two factors as interchangeable with the product.
patterns.notes: A multiple of 3, 5, 7 or 9; the range holds exactly two multiples, one even and one odd, and the parity clue picks one. The answer is the smaller or the larger, at random. Numbers below 100.

patterns.text: Which pair is a factor pair of {r.n}?

wrong.mistake: checks only that one number goes into the product
checks only that one number goes into the product
picks numbers close to a factor pair without multiplying to check

patterns.hint: Multiply each pair. Which pair gives exactly {r.n}?
patterns.explanation: {r.a} × {r.b} = {r.n}, so {r.a} and {r.b} is a factor pair of {r.n}.
patterns.misconception: Tests only one clue or treats the two factors as interchangeable with the product.
patterns.notes: 53 products from 12 to 96 with a factor pair of numbers 2 to 12; the wrong pairs are each one away and never multiply to the product.

patterns.text: Triangle × square = {a * b}, and triangle = {a}. Find square. Then find triangle + square. Give square first, then the sum.
patterns.hint: Which number times {a} makes {a * b}?
patterns.explanation: {a} × {b} = {a * b}, so square = {b}. Triangle + square = {a} + {b} = {a + b}.
patterns.misconception: Tests only one clue or treats the two factors as interchangeable with the product.
patterns.notes: Factors 3 to 12, different.

patterns.text: {a} × {b} = {a * b}. Without multiplying again, what is {b} × {a}?
patterns.hint: Changing the order of the factors does not change the product.
patterns.explanation: {a} × {b} = {a * b}, and {b} × {a} is the same: {a * b}.
patterns.misconception: Thinks changing factor order changes the product, or that multiplying by zero leaves the number unchanged.
patterns.notes: Factors 6 to 19, different.

patterns.hint: Which number times {a} gives {a * b}? Order doesn't matter.

patterns.text: Multiply: {n} × {p:num}.
patterns.hint: Multiplying by {p:num} moves every digit {num_digits(p) - 1} {'place' if p == 10 else 'places'} to the left.
patterns.explanation: {n} × {p:num} = {n * p:num}.
patterns.misconception: Appends zeroes mechanically without understanding place value, especially when the number already contains zeroes.
patterns.notes: A two-digit number times 10, 100 or 1,000.

patterns.text: Complete: {n * p:num} ÷ {p:num} = □.
patterns.hint: Think: what times {p:num} gives {n * p:num}?
patterns.explanation: {n} × {p:num} = {n * p:num}, so {n * p:num} ÷ {p:num} = {n}.
patterns.misconception: Appends zeroes mechanically without understanding place value, especially when the number already contains zeroes.
patterns.notes: As S03-P1, worked backwards.

patterns.explanation: {n} × {p:num} = {n * p:num}. {who.name} wrote {said:num}.

patterns.notes: A two-digit number times 100 or 1,000; the claimed answer is ten times too small, ten times too large or right, at random.

patterns.responseFormat: Two integers separated by a semicolon
patterns.text: A dairy packs {n} {item.what} in each {item.one}. How many {item.what} are in {p:num} {item.p}? How many are in {p * 10:num} {item.p}? Give both answers in order.
patterns.hint: Multiplying by {p * 10:num} is the same as multiplying by {p:num} and then by 10.
patterns.explanation: {n} × {p:num} = {n * p:num}; {n} × {p * 10:num} = {n * p * 10:num}.
patterns.misconception: Appends zeroes mechanically without understanding place value, especially when the number already contains zeroes.
patterns.notes: 12 to 95 per pack; 10 and 100 packs, or 100 and 1,000 packs.

patterns.text: Find {x:num} × {y:num}.
patterns.hint: Multiply {a} × {b}, then put on the zeroes from both factors.
patterns.explanation: {a} × {b} = {a * b}. The factors have {i + j} {'zero' if i + j == 1 else 'zeroes'} between them, so {x:num} × {y:num} = {x * y:num}.
patterns.misconception: Counts visible zeroes incorrectly or multiplies only the zeroes.
patterns.notes: Single digits 2 to 9 with 0 to 3 zeroes each; 1 to 4 zeroes in all.

patterns.text: Which expression equals {r.t}?

wrong.mistake: counts one zero too few
counts one zero too many
adds the numbers instead of multiplying

patterns.hint: Multiply the non-zero digits, then count the zeroes in both factors.
patterns.explanation: {r.c} = {r.t}: the digits give {r.ab} and the factors have {r.z} zeroes.
patterns.misconception: Counts visible zeroes incorrectly or multiplies only the zeroes.
patterns.notes: 120 expressions with single digits 2 to 9 and 2 to 4 zeroes between the factors.

patterns.text: How many zeroes are at the end of the product {x:num} × {y:num}?
patterns.hint: Work out {a} × {b} first. Does that product end in a zero too?
patterns.explanation: {x:num} × {y:num} = {x * y:num}, which ends in {z} zeroes.
patterns.misconception: Counts visible zeroes incorrectly or multiplies only the zeroes.
patterns.notes: Single digits 2 to 9 with 1 to 3 and 1 to 2 zeroes; about one in five copies has a digit product ending in 0 (such as 5 × 4 = 20), which adds a zero.

patterns.responseFormat: Two integers separated by a semicolon
patterns.text: A school orders {a * 10} crates of milk. Each crate holds {b * 10} packets, and each packet costs ₹{p}. How many packets are there? What is the total cost in rupees? Give both answers in order.
patterns.hint: Multiply the digits and count the zeroes. Then multiply by the price.
patterns.misconception: Counts visible zeroes incorrectly or multiplies only the zeroes.
patterns.notes: 20 to 90 crates of 20 to 90 packets at ₹2 to ₹9 each.

patterns.text: Use splitting: {a} × {b} = {a} × {10 * t} + {a} × {o}. Find the product.
patterns.hint: Find each part, then add: {a} × {10 * t} and {a} × {o}.
patterns.misconception: Omits a partial product or ignores the place value of tens and hundreds.
patterns.notes: A two-digit number 12 to 59 times 11 to 39 (not a multiple of 10).

patterns.text: Complete the missing partial product: {a} × {b} = {a * 10 * t:num} + □.
patterns.hint: {a * 10 * t:num} is {a} × {10 * t}. What is left of {b}?
patterns.explanation: {b} = {10 * t} + {o}, so the missing part is {a} × {o} = {a * o}.
patterns.misconception: Omits a partial product or ignores the place value of tens and hundreds.
patterns.notes: As S05-P1.

patterns.hint: {r.b} = {r.t} + {r.b - r.t}. Which part of {r.b} has not been multiplied by {r.a}?
patterns.explanation: {r.b} = {r.t} + {r.b - r.t}. The learner found {r.a} × {r.t} but left out {r.c}.
patterns.misconception: Omits a partial product or ignores the place value of tens and hundreds.
patterns.notes: 120 products of 12 to 59 and 12 to 39 (the ones digit 2 to 9).

patterns.text: Find {a} × {b} by splitting both numbers: ({10 * at} + {ao}) × ({10 * bt} + {bo}). Show the four partial products in your working, then add them.

steps.text: The four partial products: {10 * at} × {10 * bt} = {100 * at * bt:num}, {10 * at} × {bo} = {10 * at * bo}, {ao} × {10 * bt} = {10 * ao * bt}, {ao} × {bo} = {ao * bo}.

patterns.hint: Multiply each part of {a} by each part of {b}: four products in all.
patterns.explanation: {100 * at * bt:num} + {10 * at * bo} + {10 * ao * bt} + {ao * bo} = {a * b:num}.
patterns.misconception: Omits a partial product or ignores the place value of tens and hundreds.
patterns.notes: Two-digit numbers 21 to 79 and 11 to 49, neither a multiple of 10.

patterns.hint: {2 * a} × {h} may be easier to work out.

patterns.notes: A number 11 to 35 times an even number 6 to 18.

patterns.text: Find {a} × 25 by halving {a} twice and doubling 25 twice. Show the steps in your working.
patterns.hint: Halve {a} and double 25. Do it again.
patterns.misconception: Doubles or halves both factors and assumes the product remains unchanged.

patterns.text: Use a nearest multiple: {a} × {m - 1} = {a} × {m} − {a}. Find the product.
patterns.hint: Find {a} × {m} first, then take away one group of {a}.
patterns.misconception: Uses the nearby product but forgets or reverses the compensation.

patterns.text: Calculate {a} × {n} by using {a} × 100.
patterns.hint: {n} is {abs(n - 100)} {'more' if n > 100 else 'less'} than 100.
patterns.explanation: {a} × 100 = {a * 100:num}. {'Add' if n > 100 else 'Take away'} {abs(n - 100)} {'group' if abs(n - 100) == 1 else 'groups'} of {a}: {a * n:num}.
patterns.misconception: Uses the nearby product but forgets or reverses the compensation.

wrong.mistake: uses the nearby product but adjusts in the wrong direction

patterns.hint: {r.n} is {r.d} {r.dir} than {r.m}. How many groups of {r.a} does that change?
patterns.explanation: {r.n} is {r.d} {r.dir} than {r.m}, so {r.a} × {r.n} = {r.c}.
patterns.misconception: Uses the nearby product but forgets or reverses the compensation.
patterns.notes: 120 cases: 4 to 15 times a number 1 or 2 above or below 20, 30, 40, 50 or 60; whether to add or take away varies.

patterns.text: A shop sells {a} {item} at ₹{100 * h - 1} each. Use ₹{100 * h} and adjust to find the total. Show the adjustment in your working.
patterns.hint: Each price is ₹1 less than ₹{100 * h}.
patterns.explanation: {a} × ₹{100 * h} = {a * 100 * h:money}. Each one is ₹1 less, so take away ₹{a}: {a * (100 * h - 1):money}.
patterns.misconception: Uses the nearby product but forgets or reverses the compensation.

patterns.hint: Multiply the tens and the ones separately, then add.
patterns.misconception: Regroups without carrying the correct place value or multiplies only one digit.
patterns.notes: 12 to 98 (not a multiple of 10) times 3 to 9.

patterns.text: Find the missing partial product: {a} × {b} = {(a - a % 10) * b} + □.
patterns.hint: {(a - a % 10) * b} is {a - a % 10} × {b}. What is left?
patterns.explanation: {a} = {a - a % 10} + {a % 10}, so the missing part is {a % 10} × {b} = {a % 10 * b}.
patterns.misconception: Regroups without carrying the correct place value or multiplies only one digit.
patterns.notes: As S08-P1.

patterns.hint: Multiply the ones and carry the tens before multiplying the tens.
patterns.misconception: Regroups without carrying the correct place value or multiplies only one digit.
patterns.notes: 13 to 98 times 3 to 9, always with a carry from the ones. The right answer is the largest, the second or the third option by size, at random.

patterns.text: A dairy packs {a} pouches in each crate and fills {b} crates. It sends {s} {'crate' if s == 1 else 'crates'} to a school. How many pouches are left?

steps.text: Finds the crates left, {b} − {s} = {b - s}, or the pouches packed, {a} × {b} = {a * b}.
{a} × {b - s} = {a * (b - s)} pouches (or {a * b} − {a * s} = {a * (b - s)}).

patterns.hint: Work out how many crates are left first.
patterns.explanation: {b} − {s} = {b - s} crates are left. {a} × {b - s} = {a * (b - s)} pouches.
patterns.misconception: Regroups without carrying the correct place value or multiplies only one digit.
patterns.notes: 12 to 75 pouches a crate, 4 to 9 crates, 1 or more sent (at least 2 left).

patterns.text: Multiply: {a} × {b}.
patterns.hint: Find {a} × {b % 10} and {a} × {b - b % 10}, then add.
patterns.misconception: Omits the tens partial product or fails to shift it one place left.
patterns.notes: 21 to 79 times 12 to 39, neither a multiple of 10.

patterns.text: To find {a} × {b}, split {b} into {b - b % 10} + {b % 10}. What is the {w.k} partial product?
patterns.answer: a * (b - b % 10) if w.t == 1 else a * (b % 10)
patterns.hint: The {w.k} partial product is {a} times the {w.k} part of {b}.
patterns.explanation: {b} = {b - b % 10} + {b % 10}. The {w.k} partial product is {a} × {b - b % 10 if w.t == 1 else b % 10} = {a * (b - b % 10) if w.t == 1 else a * (b % 10):num}.
patterns.misconception: Omits the tens partial product or fails to shift it one place left.
patterns.notes: 21 to 79 times 12 to 49; asks for the tens or the ones partial product.

patterns.text: Choose the product {a} × {b}.

wrong.mistake: writes the tens partial product without shifting it one place left
leaves out the ones partial product

wrong.expr: pr + a if up == 1 else pr - a
wrong.mistake: uses one group too many or too few

patterns.hint: Find both partial products and add them.
patterns.explanation: {a} × {b % 10} = {a * (b % 10)} and {a} × {b - b % 10} = {noones:num}. {a * (b % 10)} + {noones:num} = {pr:num}.
patterns.misconception: Omits the tens partial product or fails to shift it one place left.
patterns.notes: 21 to 79 times 21 to 49, neither a multiple of 10.

patterns.text: An auditorium has {a} rows with {b} seats in each row. For a show, {s} seats are empty. How many people are seated?
patterns.hint: Find the number of seats first.
patterns.explanation: {a} × {b} = {a * b:num} seats. {a * b:num} − {s} = {a * b - s:num} people.
patterns.misconception: Omits the tens partial product or fails to shift it one place left.
patterns.notes: 18 to 45 rows of 14 to 38 seats; 12 to 95 empty.

patterns.text: Multiply: {a} × {b}.
patterns.hint: Multiply the ones, the tens and the hundreds, carrying as you go.
patterns.misconception: Skips an internal zero or carries to the wrong place.
patterns.notes: 102 to 899 (not a multiple of 10) times 2 to 9.

patterns.text: Find the {w.k} partial product in {a} × {b}.
patterns.hint: The {w.k} digit of {a} stands for {digit(a, w.p) * w.p}.
patterns.explanation: The {w.k} part of {a} is {digit(a, w.p) * w.p}. {digit(a, w.p) * w.p} × {b} = {digit(a, w.p) * w.p * b:num}.
patterns.misconception: Skips an internal zero or carries to the wrong place.
patterns.notes: As S10-P1; asks for the hundreds or the tens partial product.

patterns.notes: A three-digit number with a zero in the tens place (101 to 809) times 2 to 9; the right answer is the largest or second smallest at random.

patterns.text: {v} farmers each bring {b} cans of milk to a cooperative. {d} cans are found leaking and are not used. How many cans are used?
patterns.hint: Find the number of cans brought first.
patterns.explanation: {v} × {b} = {v * b:num}. {v * b:num} − {d} = {v * b - d:num}.
patterns.misconception: Skips an internal zero or carries to the wrong place.
patterns.notes: 105 to 480 farmers, 3 to 9 cans each, 12 to 96 leaking.

patterns.explanation: {a} × {b % 10} = {a * (b % 10):num}; {a} × {b - b % 10} = {noones:num}. Total: {pr:num}.
patterns.misconception: Treats tens or hundreds in the multiplier as ones.
patterns.notes: 102 to 399 times 21 to 49.

patterns.text: A dairy has {c} cows. Each gives {l} litres of milk a day. The dairy sells {s:num} litres to a sweet shop. How many litres are left?

steps.text: Milk in a day: {c} × {l} = {c * l:num} litres.

patterns.hint: Find the day's milk first.
patterns.explanation: {c} × {l} = {c * l:num} litres. {c * l:num} − {s:num} = {c * l - s:num} litres.
patterns.misconception: Treats tens or hundreds in the multiplier as ones.
patterns.notes: 105 to 399 cows at 11 to 19 litres; 105 to 995 litres sold.

patterns.text: Estimate {a} × {b} by rounding both factors to the nearest ten.
patterns.hint: Round {a} and {b} to the nearest ten, then multiply.
patterns.explanation: {a} is about {round_half_up(a, 10)} and {b} is about {round_half_up(b, 10)}. {round_half_up(a, 10)} × {round_half_up(b, 10)} = {round_half_up(a, 10) * round_half_up(b, 10):num}.
patterns.misconception: Accepts an exact-looking answer without comparing its size with an estimate.
patterns.notes: Two-digit factors 12 to 98, not ending in 0 or 5.

values.name: w3
values.expr: a * (b - b % 10) if up == 0 else pr + 10 * a

patterns.text: Before calculating {a} × {b}, an estimate is {est:num}. Which exact answer could be right?

wrong.mistake: puts in an extra zero
loses a place value

patterns.hint: Compare each answer with the estimate. The right one has to be close to {est:num}.
patterns.explanation: {a} × {b} = {pr:num}, close to the estimate {est:num}. The others are ten times too big or too small, or far from it.
patterns.misconception: Accepts an exact-looking answer without comparing its size with an estimate.
patterns.notes: Two-digit factors 21 to 98 not ending in 0 or 5.

patterns.text: The exact product {a} × {b} is {a * b:num}, and the estimate by rounding to tens is {est:num}. What is the difference between them?
patterns.hint: Take the smaller number away from the larger.
patterns.explanation: The difference between {a * b:num} and {est:num} is {abs(a * b - est):num}.
patterns.misconception: Accepts an exact-looking answer without comparing its size with an estimate.
patterns.notes: As S12-P2.

patterns.text: {who.name} reports {r.a} × {r.b} = {r.claim}. What most likely happened?

wrong.mistake: doesn't compare the answer with an estimate
doesn't compare the answer with an estimate
doesn't compare the answer with an estimate

steps.text: Estimates {r.a} × {r.b} as about {r.est} (exact: {r.p}) and compares {r.claim} with it.

patterns.hint: Estimate first, then compare. Is {r.claim} far from the estimate?
patterns.explanation: {r.a} × {r.b} = {r.p} (about {r.est}). {who.name} wrote {r.claim}: {r.c}.
patterns.misconception: Accepts an exact-looking answer without comparing its size with an estimate.
patterns.notes: Two-digit factors not ending in 0 or 5; the claimed answer is ten times too big, the tens partial product only, the sum, or right, so the right choice varies.

patterns.text: Given {r.a} × {r.b} = {r.p:num}, find {r.q} without starting again.
patterns.hint: How many groups have been added or taken away?
patterns.explanation: To get {r.q} from {r.a} × {r.b}, {r.how}: {r.p:num} → {r.ans:num}.
patterns.misconception: Adds the changed factor instead of the unchanged factor when one factor increases by one.
patterns.notes: Factors 11 to 30 and 11 to 35; the second factor goes up or down by 1, or the first goes up by 1.

patterns.text: Given {a} × {b} = {a * b:num}, find {2 * a} × {h}.
patterns.hint: Compare the factors: one is doubled and one is halved.
patterns.explanation: {2 * a} × {h} doubles {a} and halves {b}, so the product stays {a * b:num}.
patterns.misconception: Adds the changed factor instead of the unchanged factor when one factor increases by one.
patterns.notes: 11 to 30 times an even number 12 to 36.

patterns.text: {r.a} × {r.b} = {r.p:num}. Which number must be added to {r.p:num} to find {r.q}?

wrong.mistake: adds the factor that changed instead of the one that stayed
thinks one more in a factor adds one to the product
adds both factors

patterns.hint: Which factor went up by 1? That adds one more group of the other factor.
patterns.explanation: {r.q} is {r.why}, so add {r.c}: {r.p:num} + {r.c} = {r.p + r.c:num}.
patterns.misconception: Adds the changed factor instead of the unchanged factor when one factor increases by one.
patterns.notes: Factors 11 to 30 and 11 to 35; either factor goes up by 1, so the right number to add varies.

patterns.responseFormat: Two integers separated by a semicolon
patterns.text: Use {a} × 100 = {a * 100:num} to find {a} × 99 and {a} × 101. Give both answers in order.
patterns.hint: 99 is one group fewer than 100; 101 is one group more.
patterns.misconception: Adds the changed factor instead of the unchanged factor when one factor increases by one.

patterns.text: Look at the pattern: 11 × {n - 2} = {11 * (n - 2)}, 11 × {n - 1} = {11 * (n - 1)}, 11 × {n} = □. What number goes in the box?
patterns.hint: Each product is 11 more than the one before. Or: 11 × {n} = {n} × 10 + {n}.
patterns.explanation: 11 × {n} = {n * 10} + {n} = {11 * n:num}, which is 11 more than {11 * (n - 1)}.
patterns.misconception: Extends a visible digit pattern without checking the multiplication rule.
patterns.notes: 12 to 98, not a multiple of 10.

patterns.text: A reward box has {s} coins at the start of day 1. At the end of every day, the number of coins is {m.w}. How many coins are in the box at the end of day {d}?
patterns.hint: Multiply by {m.k} once for each day, from day 1 to day {d}.
patterns.explanation: {s} coins, multiplied by {m.k} at the end of each of the {d} days: {s * m.k ** d:num} coins at the end of day {d}.
patterns.misconception: Extends a visible digit pattern without checking the multiplication rule.
patterns.notes: 2 to 6 coins, doubled or tripled, for 2 to 5 days (at most 1,458).

patterns.text: A sequence is {r.s}, {r.t2}, {r.t3:num}, {r.t4:num}, ... What is the rule?

wrong.mistake: checks only the first two terms
uses the first term as the multiplier
sees the multiplier but adds it

patterns.hint: Check the rule on every pair of terms, not just the first two.
patterns.explanation: Each term is {r.m} times the one before: {r.s} × {r.m} = {r.t2}, {r.t2} × {r.m} = {r.t3}.
patterns.misconception: Extends a visible digit pattern without checking the multiplication rule.
patterns.notes: 21 sequences starting at 2 to 9, multiplied by 2 to 5.

patterns.responseFormat: Two integers separated by a semicolon
patterns.text: Find {a} × {a} and {a + 1} × {a + 1}. Give both answers in order.
patterns.hint: Multiply each number by itself.
patterns.misconception: Extends a visible digit pattern without checking the multiplication rule.

patterns.text: A farm has {c} cows. Each gives {l} litres of milk a day. How many litres are collected in one day?
patterns.hint: Each cow gives {l} litres. Multiply by the number of cows.
patterns.explanation: {c} × {l} = {c * l:num} litres.
patterns.misconception: Multiplies every number shown or stops before completing all requested steps.
patterns.notes: 18 to 96 cows at 6 to 14 litres.

patterns.text: A shop sells {n1} {it.x} at ₹{p1} each and {n2} {it.y} at ₹{p2} each. What is the total bill in rupees?
patterns.hint: Find the cost of each kind, then add.
patterns.explanation: {n1} × ₹{p1} = {n1 * p1:money}; {n2} × ₹{p2} = {n2 * p2:money}. Total: {n1 * p1 + n2 * p2:money}.
patterns.misconception: Multiplies every number shown or stops before completing all requested steps.
patterns.notes: 11 to 25 of each item at ₹12 to ₹45.

patterns.text: A farm has {r.c} cows, each giving {r.l} litres a day. Which plan finds {r.q}?

wrong.mistake: uses a plan that answers a different question
uses a plan that answers a different question
adds every number shown

patterns.hint: Say in words what the question asks, then choose the operations in that order.
patterns.explanation: To find {r.q}, the plan is {r.cc}.
patterns.misconception: Multiplies every number shown or stops before completing all requested steps.
patterns.notes: 24 to 87 cows at 6 to 12 litres; three kinds of question (days, milk sold, more cows), so the right plan varies.

patterns.text: A farm has {c} cows, each giving {l} litres of milk a day. Milk sells at ₹{p} a litre. How much money does the farm get from {d} days' milk?

steps.text: Milk in {d} days: {c} × {l} × {d} = {c * l * d:num} litres (or money in a day: {c * l * p:money}).

patterns.hint: Find the litres first, then the money.
patterns.explanation: {c} × {l} = {c * l} litres a day; × {d} days = {c * l * d:num} litres; × ₹{p} = {c * l * d * p:money}.
patterns.misconception: Multiplies every number shown or stops before completing all requested steps.
patterns.notes: 12 to 30 cows at 8 to 14 litres, ₹40 to ₹60 a litre, 2 to 5 days.

patterns.text: Find {a} × {b} by splitting {b} into tens and ones. Show both partial products and add them.
patterns.answer: {a} × {bo} = {a * bo:num}. {a} × {10 * bt} = {a * 10 * bt:num}. {a * bo:num} + {a * 10 * bt:num} = {a * b:num}.

steps.text: Tens partial product: {a} × {10 * bt} = {a * 10 * bt:num} (ending in zero).
Adds: {a * b:num}. Follow through from a slip in one partial product if the method is right.

patterns.explanation: {a} × {b} = {a * bo:num} + {a * 10 * bt:num} = {a * b:num}.
patterns.misconception: Treats tens or hundreds in the multiplier as ones.
patterns.notes: 105 to 499 times 22 to 49 (not a multiple of 10).

patterns.text: {who.name} says {a} × {b} = {claim:num}. Estimate the product, explain why {who.his} answer is not reasonable, and find the correct product.
patterns.answer: Estimate: {round_half_up(a, 10)} × {round_half_up(b, 10)} = {est:num}. {claim:num} is about ten times {'smaller' if k == 0 else 'bigger'} than the estimate, so it can't be right. Correct product: {a} × {b} = {pr:num}.

steps.text: Explains: {claim:num} is about ten times {'smaller' if k == 0 else 'bigger'} than {est:num}, so a place value has been {'lost' if k == 0 else 'added'}.

patterns.hint: Round both numbers to the nearest ten and multiply. Is {claim:num} close?
patterns.explanation: {a} × {b} is about {est:num}, so {claim:num} is far off. The product is {pr:num}.
patterns.misconception: Accepts an exact-looking answer without comparing its size with an estimate.
patterns.notes: Two-digit factors 21 to 98 not ending in 0 or 5; the claim is ten times too small or too big.

patterns.text: A farm has {c1} cows giving {l1} litres of milk each a day and {c2} buffaloes giving {l2} litres each a day. How many litres of milk does the farm get in a day? Show your working.
patterns.answer: Cows: {c1} × {l1} = {c1 * l1} litres. Buffaloes: {c2} × {l2} = {c2 * l2} litres. Total: {c1 * l1} + {c2 * l2} = {c1 * l1 + c2 * l2:num} litres.

steps.text: Adds: {c1 * l1 + c2 * l2:num} litres, with the unit. Follow through from a slip.

patterns.hint: Find the cows' milk and the buffaloes' milk separately, then add.
patterns.explanation: {c1 * l1} + {c2 * l2} = {c1 * l1 + c2 * l2:num} litres.
patterns.misconception: Multiplies every number shown or stops before completing all requested steps.
patterns.notes: 12 to 48 cows at 8 to 14 litres; 6 to 25 buffaloes at 5 to 9 litres.

patterns.text: A dairy has {c} cows. Each gives {l} litres of milk a day. Milk sells at ₹{p} a litre, and the dairy spends {e:money} a day on feed. (a) How many litres does it get in a day? (b) How much money does that milk bring? (c) How much is left after paying for feed? (d) How much is left in {d} days? (e) Check (b) with an estimate. Show your working.
patterns.answer: (a) {c} × {l} = {c * l} litres. (b) {c * l} × ₹{p} = {c * l * p:money}. (c) {c * l * p:money} − {e:money} = {c * l * p - e:money}. (d) {c * l * p - e:money} × {d} = {(c * l * p - e) * d:money}. (e) About {round_half_up(c * l, 10)} × {round_half_up(p, 10)} = {round_half_up(c * l, 10) * round_half_up(p, 10):money}, close to {c * l * p:money}.

steps.text: (d) {c * l * p - e:money} × {d} = {(c * l * p - e) * d:money}.
(e) A sensible estimate, such as {round_half_up(c * l, 10)} × {round_half_up(p, 10)} = {round_half_up(c * l, 10) * round_half_up(p, 10):money}, compared with (b).

patterns.hint: Work in order: litres, then money, then take away the feed, then multiply by the days.
patterns.explanation: {c * l} litres bring {c * l * p:money}; after feed, {c * l * p - e:money} a day; in {d} days, {(c * l * p - e) * d:money}.
patterns.misconception: Multiplies every number shown or stops before completing all requested steps.
patterns.notes: 15 to 45 cows at 8 to 12 litres; ₹40 to ₹56 a litre; feed ₹2,000 to ₹6,000 a day (at least ₹1,000 left); 3 to 7 days.

patterns.text: For {a} × {b}: (a) estimate the product by rounding both numbers to the nearest ten; (b) find {a} × {b % 10}; (c) find {a} × {b - b % 10}; (d) add them to get the exact product; (e) find the difference between the estimate and the exact product. Show your working.
patterns.answer: (a) {round_half_up(a, 10)} × {round_half_up(b, 10)} = {round_half_up(a, 10) * round_half_up(b, 10):num}. (b) {a} × {b % 10} = {a * (b % 10)}. (c) {a} × {b - b % 10} = {a * (b - b % 10):num}. (d) {a * (b % 10)} + {a * (b - b % 10):num} = {a * b:num}. (e) {abs(a * b - round_half_up(a, 10) * round_half_up(b, 10)):num}.
patterns.hint: Do the estimate first. Then the two partial products.
patterns.explanation: Estimate {round_half_up(a, 10) * round_half_up(b, 10):num}; exact {a * b:num}; difference {abs(a * b - round_half_up(a, 10) * round_half_up(b, 10)):num}.
patterns.misconception: Omits the tens partial product or fails to shift it one place left.
patterns.notes: Two-digit factors 23 to 98, not ending in 0 or 5.

patterns.text: Given {a} × {b} = {a * b:num}, find each of these without multiplying from the beginning, and say in one line how you got it: (a) {b} × {a} (b) {a} × {b + 1} (c) {a + 1} × {b} (d) {2 * a} × {h} (e) {a} × {b * 10}.
patterns.answer: (a) {a * b:num}: order doesn't change the product. (b) {a * b:num} + {a} = {a * b + a:num}: one more group of {a}. (c) {a * b:num} + {b} = {a * b + b:num}: one more group of {b}. (d) {a * b:num}: double one factor, halve the other. (e) {a * b * 10:num}: ten times the product.

steps.text: (a) {a * b:num}, because order doesn't change the product.
(d) {a * b:num}: doubling and halving keep the product.

patterns.hint: Think about what changed in each one compared with {a} × {b}.
patterns.explanation: (a) {a * b:num}, (b) {a * b + a:num}, (c) {a * b + b:num}, (d) {a * b:num}, (e) {a * b * 10:num}.
patterns.misconception: Adds the changed factor instead of the unchanged factor when one factor increases by one.
patterns.notes: 12 to 29 times an even number 14 to 34.
